title: Long: quarterly review, mixed signals (3 people)
transcript:
Marcus (Acme): Thanks for making time, both of you. This is our quarterly review, so I'd like to cover lead quality, the billing question Linda raised, and what next year looks like. Does that work?
Greg (Summit): That works. I'll be straight with you, Marcus, it's been a mixed quarter. Texas has been excellent. Oklahoma is fine. Louisiana has been a real problem since about mid October.
Marcus: Okay. Tell me what you're seeing in Louisiana.
Linda (Summit): So I pulled the numbers before the call. In Texas our contact rate is around 42 percent. In Louisiana it dropped from 38 percent in September to 19 percent in November. And we're getting duplicates. Last week alone we had nine leads that were the same people we bought in October.
Marcus: Nine duplicates in a week is not acceptable, and I'm sorry. That shouldn't get past our dedupe check at all.
Linda: I'll give you one example so your team can trace it. Dorothy Hale, phone 504-555-0187, email dhale1952@example.com. We got her on October 9th and again on November 18th, same annuity form, same answers.
Marcus: That's really helpful, thank you. My guess is the Louisiana campaign was moved to a new form vendor in October and their records are not running through our dedupe. I'll confirm that with our data team rather than guess.
Greg: Here's my concern. A competitor reached out last month offering exclusive annuity leads at 28 dollars. We're paying you 35. I've been loyal for two years because the quality was worth it, but if Louisiana keeps looking like this, I can't justify it to my partners.
Marcus: That's fair, and I appreciate you telling me instead of just leaving. What would you need to see?
Greg: Louisiana fixed by the end of January. Contact rate back over 30 percent and zero duplicates. If that doesn't happen, we'll move the Louisiana budget to the other vendor and keep you on Texas and Oklahoma only.
Marcus: Understood. Now the billing question.
Linda: Right. We returned 14 leads in October through the portal, all bad phone numbers or duplicates. We were told they'd be credited. The November invoice still charged us for all of them. That's 490 dollars.
Marcus: You're right, that should have been credited. I'll get the 490 dollar credit applied by this Friday and send you a corrected invoice.
Linda: Thank you. And going forward, can returns show up on the invoice as a line item? Right now I'm matching spreadsheets by hand every month.
Marcus: I'll ask billing if we can do that. I won't promise it today, but I'll tell you by our next call.
Greg: Okay. Now the good news, because there is some. Our two new agents in Houston are closing well, and Texas is carrying us. I'd like to raise Texas from 50 leads a month to 80, starting in January.
Marcus: That's great to hear. 30 more Texas leads a month is very doable. I'll send you a quote for the higher volume.
Greg: And we've been talking about final expense. Some of our agents are licensed for it. Would you do a small test, say 20 final expense leads in Texas, just to see?
Marcus: Yes, we can run a 20 lead pilot. I'll put a proposal together with pricing, and we can start it alongside the Texas increase.
Linda: One more thing on operations. Our appointment no shows are up. Could your team send the appointment reminder text the morning of, instead of the night before?
Marcus: We can change that setting on your account. I'll have it switched to morning reminders this week.
Greg: Good. So to sum up, Louisiana is the thing that decides whether we stay at full volume. Everything else is going well.
Marcus: Got it. Let me play back what I've got. I'll get the 490 dollar credit applied by Friday. I'll have the data team trace the Louisiana duplicates and send you a written root cause by December 12th. Morning reminders this week. A quote for 80 Texas leads and a final expense pilot proposal by next Wednesday. Linda, could you send me the full list of the nine duplicates?
Linda: I'll send the list today.
Marcus: And let's book a check in for January 15th to look at the Louisiana numbers together.
Greg: January 15th works. Thanks, Marcus.
Marcus: Thank you both. Talk soon.

title: Long: consent complaint, renewal at risk
transcript:
Marcus (Acme): Hi Ruth, thanks for calling. My notes say you wanted to talk about a consumer complaint?
Ruth (Golden Years): Yes, and I'll be honest, I'm upset. On Monday one of my agents called a lead from your feed, a Mr. Albert Kessler, and he told her he never filled out any form. He threatened to report us. Then on Wednesday a second person said the same thing.
Marcus: I'm sorry, that's serious. Thank you for bringing it straight to me.
Ruth: Serious is the right word. If we're calling people without consent, that's a TCPA problem, and the fines are per call. My compliance person says one lawsuit could cost more than everything we've ever spent with you.
Marcus: I understand. Every lead we sell should have a consent record: the form, the time stamp, the IP address and the exact consent wording they agreed to. I can pull those records for both leads today.
Ruth: I want more than those two. I want consent records for every lead you've sent us since September. That's about 360 leads.
Marcus: That's a reasonable ask. I'll need to check how quickly we can export that many, but you'll have them. Let me give you a date after I talk to the compliance team this afternoon.
Ruth: And I need to know where these leads came from. Were they bought from someone else and resold to us?
Marcus: Our final expense leads come from our own forms, but in October we added a partner site to fill volume in Tennessee. If these two came from that partner, I'll find out and tell you plainly.
Ruth: They were both Tennessee numbers.
Marcus: Then that's where I'll look first. Until I know, I'll pause the partner traffic on your account so you only get leads from our own forms.
Ruth: Do that today, please. Not next week.
Marcus: Today. I'll email you when it's done.
Ruth: There's something else. My best agent quit two weeks ago, so I'm down to three people. Honestly, even before this, I wasn't sure I could use 120 leads a month.
Marcus: Would it help to drop to a smaller plan for a while? I'd rather you have fewer leads you can work than leads going cold.
Ruth: Maybe. Let's not talk about that until the consent thing is settled. Our renewal is in February, and I'm not renewing unless I see clean consent records for every lead.
Marcus: That's completely fair. I'll make sure you have everything well before February.
Ruth: Also, my office manager asked me to give you the new card for billing, since the old one expired. It's 4111 1111 1111 1111, expiry 09 28.
Marcus: Thank you. Actually, please don't read card numbers on calls. They get recorded. I'll send you a secure payment link instead, and please ignore the number you just read, I won't use it.
Ruth: Oh. Fine, send the link.
Marcus: I'll send the payment link right after this call. To recap: consent records for the two complaints today, the partner traffic paused today, and a date for the full export of all leads since September once I've spoken to compliance.
Ruth: And a written answer on where those two leads came from.
Marcus: Yes, a written answer on the source of both leads by Friday.
Ruth: Okay. I'm not happy, Marcus, but I appreciate that you're not dodging it.
Marcus: I understand. I'll call you Friday either way, even if I don't have every answer yet.
Ruth: Fine. Talk Friday.

title: Long: expansion, webinar trial, GHL setup (3 people)
transcript:
Priya (Acme): Good morning, Dev. Good morning, Sam. Thanks for setting this up. You said you wanted to talk about growth for next year?
Dev (Northstar): Morning, Priya. Yes. 2026 was our best year so far, and a big part of that was your retirement planning leads. We booked 61 seminar seats from your leads in Illinois last quarter alone.
Priya: That's wonderful. What's working best for you?
Dev: The seminar registration leads. People who sign up for a dinner seminar show up, and they're ready to talk. The plain web form leads are fine, but the seminar ones close at about twice the rate.
Sam (Northstar): That said, Wisconsin is a different story. Our show rate at the Milwaukee events dropped to around 45 percent. In Illinois it's closer to 70.
Priya: Do you have a sense of why?
Sam: Two things, I think. The reminder texts go out two days before, and people forget. And the Milwaukee venue changed in October, so some people went to the old address.
Priya: The venue I can fix today on our side. I'll update the event details in every reminder. And we could add a second reminder, the morning of the event. Would that help?
Sam: Yes, please. Both of those.
Dev: Now the bigger topic. We're opening an office in Minneapolis in February. We'd like seminar leads for Minnesota from day one, about 40 a month.
Priya: Congratulations. Minnesota is in your plan's region, so that's straightforward. I'll send you a quote for 40 Minnesota seminar leads a month.
Dev: We're also curious about your webinar product. Some of our older prospects in rural areas won't drive an hour to a dinner. What does that cost?
Priya: Webinar registrations are 22 dollars a lead, and the seminar ones are 45.
Dev: Hmm. 22 is fine, but we've never tried webinars, so I don't want to commit to big volume. Could we do a trial?
Priya: We can do a trial. How about 50 webinar leads over six weeks, and if your cost per appointment is worse than the seminars, you stop with no penalty.
Dev: That's fair. Let's do it.
Sam: The last piece is operational. We moved our calendar to Go High Level last month. Right now someone on my team copies every registration from your email into our calendar by hand. That's about five hours a week.
Priya: We can send registrations straight to your Go High Level account, so they land on the right calendar with the lead's details. I'll need an API key from you, and our integration team will set it up.
Sam: I'll send the API key through your secure portal, not email.
Priya: Perfect, thank you. Once we have it, setup usually takes about a week.
Dev: One honest concern. When we grow this fast, quality usually drops. I don't want 40 Minnesota leads a month if half are junk.
Priya: That's fair. Let's start Minnesota at 25 a month for the first month, review the contact and show rates together, and step up to 40 if the numbers hold.
Dev: I like that better.
Priya: Great. So my list is: fix the Milwaukee venue in the reminders today, add a morning of reminder, a quote for Minnesota starting at 25 and stepping up to 40, set up the 50 lead webinar trial, and the Go High Level integration once Sam sends the key. I'll send the quote and the trial terms by Thursday.
Sam: And I'll send the key this week.
Dev: Sounds like a plan. Thanks, Priya.
Priya: Thank you both. Talk soon.
